prof.hint: Per-file profit & loss for direct (own-account) business: revenue − cost = gross profit, built from charge lines on the shipment. Agency business (billed per cycle, not per file) and per-container P&L are excluded — see the notes in migration 021.
prof.kpiGpHelp: Sum of (revenue − cost) across all direct files that have both revenue and cost recorded.
prof.kpiLossHelp: Files where cost exceeded revenue. Drill in to see whether it's pricing, a cost overrun, or under-billing.
prof.trendHelp: Bars = gross profit by month (by shipment ETA, falling back to file open date); line = margin %.
prof.topCustHelp: Direct customers ranked by total gross profit over all history.
prof.topOperHelp: Gross profit on the files each operator handled.

kpi.openReceivablesHelp: Total unpaid invoice balance across all customers (freight + duty), excluding related parties and voided invoices. This is the current live figure, not a period snapshot.
kpi.overdueByBaselineHelp: Open balance from customers who are past their OWN historical payment pace — not the nominal due date. 57% of invoices carry zero-day terms and the on-time rate is only 20%, so the nominal date would flag 80% of invoices; measuring against each customer's baseline surfaces the ones actually slipping.
kpi.creditBreachesHelp: Number of customers whose open exposure has reached their credit-limit warning threshold (default 80%). Only customers with a real limit set (≥ $100) are counted; related parties are excluded.
kpi.unrecovered12mHelp: Advanced costs that should have been billed back to the customer but were not — demurrage, detention, duty, chassis and similar — over the last 12 months, direct customers only. Agency business settles per cycle and is excluded to avoid false gaps.
kpi.billingLagMedianHelp: Median days from opening a house B/L to issuing the first invoice, over the last 12 months (direct customers). Two-thirds of the cash cycle is this internal lag — compressing it frees working capital without asking customers for anything.
kpi.unbilledFilesHelp: Direct-customer files opened ≥ 45 days ago that have costs booked but still no invoice. 45 days is the threshold because the median lag for billed files is 24 days — these are genuine exceptions, not the norm.

alerts.title: Alert workbench
alerts.intro: Aggregated action items from five rules. Drill into each page for line-level detail.
alerts.subject: Subject
alerts.rulesHint: All rules are disabled until recipients are configured and false-positive rates are reviewed.
alerts.severityHelp: Set automatically from the amount and how far past thresholds an item is — critical / serious / warning. It is not manually assigned.
alerts.amountHelp: The money at stake for this alert: open exposure, unrecovered gap, or surplus payment, depending on the rule. Some rules (e.g. billing delay) have no dollar amount.
alerts.scheduleHelp: When this rule runs, in cron format (minute hour day month weekday). Example '0 8 * * 1-5' = 08:00 on weekdays. Rules only send on their schedule, not continuously.
alerts.throttleHelp: The same alert is not re-sent within this many hours. Without it, an unchanged problem would email people every day until they mute the whole rule.
alerts.enabledStateHelp: All rules ship disabled. Turn one on only after its recipients are set and its false-positive rate has been reviewed on real data.

aging.title: Receivables ageing
aging.note: Overdue on this page is measured against each customer's own payment baseline, not the nominal due date — 57% of invoices carry zero-day terms and the on-time rate is 20%, so the nominal date would flag 80% of invoices.

recv.title: Open receivables
recv.relatedHint: Related parties are excluded from collections and credit alerts; their position is tracked here.
recv.pastDueNominalHelp: Days past the invoice's nominal due date (invoice date + terms). Use with caution: 57% of invoices carry zero-day terms, so this flags almost everything. It is the accounting/compliance view.
recv.pastBaselineHelp: Days past this customer's OWN typical payment pace (median days-to-pay from their last 4 years). This is the collections view — it surfaces customers actually slipping, not those on normal terms.
recv.dutyHelp: Advanced customs duty still owed (duty billed minus duty paid). It is zero-margin money we fronted to CBP — a different kind of exposure from freight, so it is shown separately.
recv.netHelp: Billed to them minus billed by them, per month. Negative means the related party invoiced us more than we invoiced them (we owe them net).
recv.billedToThemHelp: What we invoiced this related party (our receivable from them).
recv.billedByThemHelp: What this related party invoiced us (our payable to them).

cust.title: Customers
cust.name: Customer
cust.noBaseline: No payment history in the last 4 years
cust.utilizationHelp: Open exposure ÷ credit limit. Shown only for customers with a real limit set (≥ $100). Red at/over 100%, amber at/over the warning ratio (default 80%).
cust.medianDaysHelp: Median days from invoice to payment over this customer's last 4 years — their real payment pace, the basis for behavioural overdue.
cust.onTimeHelp: Share of this customer's invoices (last 4 years) paid on or before the nominal due date.
cust.policyHelp: The credit limit actually enforced by this system — maintained here, not in FreightStream. The source system's own limit field is unenforced and mostly empty, so it is not used.
cust.baselineHelp: How this customer actually pays, computed from their last 4 years of paid invoices. This is the basis for 'past baseline' overdue instead of the nominal due date.
cust.membersHelp: FreightStream accounts merged into this one entity. A company often has separate accounts (e.g. a main account and a '-DUTY' account); merging them shows true total exposure.
cust.historyHelp: Every change to this customer's credit policy, with who made it and when — recorded automatically and tamper-proof. Source of truth for 'who raised this limit'.
cust.openItemsHelp: Unpaid invoices for this entity. 'Past baseline' compares against the customer's own payment pace; 'past due' is against the nominal date.
cust.dutyLimitHelp: A separate ceiling for advanced customs duty. Duty is zero-margin money fronted to CBP with hard deadlines, so it is capped apart from freight exposure.
cust.warnRatioHelp: Utilisation at which this customer starts showing as a credit-limit alert. Default 80% — warns before the limit is actually breached.
cust.p90Help: 90th-percentile days-to-pay: 9 out of 10 invoices are paid within this many days. Shows the slow tail, not just the typical case.
cust.nominalTermsHelp: The payment terms most often written on this customer's invoices. Often zero — which is exactly why overdue is measured against behaviour, not this.
cust.openInvoicesHelp: Number of unpaid invoices this customer currently has open. It counts invoices, not money — see Exposure for the amount.
cust.totalOpenHelp: Exposure = total money this customer currently owes across all open invoices (freight + duty), merged across their linked accounts and excluding voided invoices. This is what you'd lose if they never paid — the number credit limits are measured against.
cust.overdueHelp: The portion of exposure that is past the customer's OWN payment baseline (their historical median days-to-pay), not the nominal due date. Exposure is everything owed; overdue is the slice that is genuinely late. A customer can have large exposure but zero overdue if nothing has aged past their normal pace.

cost.title: Cost recovery
cost.unrecoveredHint: Direct customers only. Cost is passed through two ways: a receivable invoice to the customer, and a debit to the overseas agent on a credit/debit note (CR/DB); both are netted off. What remains unmatched for agency business settled per cycle is a billing model, not leakage.
cost.duplicatesHint: Suspected duplicates to verify — not a verdict. Always check against the vendor's invoice before acting. Shows the same charge line (description + rate + qty) recorded on more than one voucher for the same vendor + invoice + shipment. ⚠ On consolidated invoices (one number spanning many shipments), the same charge is often booked in legitimate batches — look at Entry gap: near 0 usually means batch entry (same minutes); hours or days apart is more suspicious. Installments, per-quantity splits and multi-container lines are already excluded.
cost.stateHelp: Not rebilled = cost was paid but never invoiced to the customer nor debited to the agent (a genuine miss). Under-rebilled = less than 90% of the cost came back. Recovered via agent = recovered by debiting the overseas agent on a credit/debit note (CR/DB), not a miss. No customer invoice = the file has no receivable at all and no agent debit, usually agency business settled per cycle. Recovered = fully passed through. Agent partly debited = the file has no customer invoice and only part of the cost was debited to the agent. The remainder is usually a pricing structure (e.g. we pay $1,800 for a chassis and bill the agent a flat $160), so it is **not counted as a miss**; it is listed separately for a human to judge.
cost.gapHelp: Cost we paid out minus what we billed back to the customer. Positive = money not recovered.
cost.netCostHelp: Demurrage/detention/storage paid to terminals & carriers, minus what we recovered from customers. Positive = net out of pocket.
cost.recoveryPctHelp: Recovered ÷ paid-out for this charge type. Below 100% means part of the penalty was absorbed rather than passed on.
cost.recoveryPctHelp2: Recovered ÷ paid-out. The climb from ~4% to ~90% is real management improvement — but part of the early low rate is agency business (settled per cycle, no per-file AR). Filter to Direct only for the clean picture.
cost.trendHint: Click any row to drill into the individual shipments behind it. Recovery % below 100 means part of the penalty was absorbed, not passed on.
cost.dupDrillHint: Each row is one AP voucher under the same vendor + invoice. Check Rate × Qty: two rows of qty 0.5 are an installment (not a duplicate); qty 1 repeated is a real duplicate. Voided ones are reversed; non-voided are the live exposure.
cost.agentDebitHelp: Amount debited to an overseas agent or affiliate on a credit/debit note (CR/DB). This is the second path for passing cost through — versions before 2026-09-25 could not see it and therefore misread about 60% of normal business as "not rebilled" (94% for duty). Gap = cost − customer receivable − agent debit.

bill.title: Billing timeliness
bill.hint: Two-thirds of the cash cycle is internal billing lag. Threshold is 45 days because the median lag for invoiced files is 24 days — 30 would flag the norm, not the exception.
bill.medianLagHelp: Median days from opening a file to its first invoice, for files this operator DID bill in the last 12 months. Their normal billing speed.
bill.lagDaysHelp: Days from file opened to first invoice, for files already billed. Blank if not yet billed.
bill.unbilledDaysHelp: Days a still-unbilled file has been open. This is the number that matters for chasing — the clock is still running.
bill.unbilledOverHelp: Files open past the threshold, with costs already booked but no invoice — the genuine backlog. Files with no cost are excluded (usually voided or empty shells).
bill.oldestHelp: The longest any of this operator's unbilled-with-cost files has been sitting open.
bill.thresholdHelp: How many days open before an unbilled file counts as a backlog item. Default 45, because the median lag for billed files is 24 — 45 flags real exceptions, not the norm.
bill.billedHelp: Of the files this operator handled, how many already have an invoice. The rest are the unbilled backlog.

staff.title: Staff output
staff.note: Counts records CREATED per day (files / receivable invoices / payable entries). The source only stores first-create and last-modify, so this is output volume, not every action. System accounts (e.g. AMS) are excluded.
staff.clickDay: Click a day to see the records created that day.

op.hint: Five dimensions per OP, attributed by the file's operator: workload, billing speed, cost pass-through, demurrage recovery, entry quality. Every number here drills down to the actual files.
op.noScoreTitle: No composite score here, and no gross profit yet
op.noScoreBody: No single score: cargo mix and customer structure differ a lot between operators (one may handle a single large agency account, another dozens of direct customers) — a single score would read structural difference as skill difference. No per-file gross profit yet: in this ERP the operational ledger (T_OPACCT) and the financial vouchers (T_APDETAIL) each record only part of a file's cost and contradict each other; we've asked ops/finance which table is authoritative. Once confirmed, margin joins as a sixth column.
op.directFilesHelp: Direct (own-account) files and their share. The money and timing metrics below use direct files only — agency business is invoiced in batches per settlement cycle and has no per-file receivable, so mixing it in manufactures phantom gaps (one operator showed 524 files "unbilled >45 days" on the full population, but only 5 on direct). So for anyone with a low direct share, the metrics to the right cover only part of their actual work.
op.medLagHelp: Median days from file opened to first invoice, direct files only. The 24-month database-wide median is 24 days, so above 45 days is red and 30–45 amber. Median, not mean: a handful of files dragging half a year would wreck the mean.
op.unbilled45Help: Direct files that have incurred payable cost, still have no receivable invoice at all, and were opened more than 45 days ago. The "has cost" condition matters: of 8,093 unbilled files database-wide only 3,910 have any cost — the rest are mostly void or empty shells, and chasing them is pointless.
op.unrecGapHelp: Costs that should have been rebilled to the customer (customs, demurrage, storage…) but were not, or only partly — direct files only. **There are two paths for passing cost through**: a receivable invoice to the customer, and a debit to the overseas agent on a credit/debit note (CR/DB); both are netted off here. Versions before 2026-09-25 could not see the agent path and misread about 60% of normal business as not rebilled. Drill in to see which files and which charge class.
op.demRecoveryHelp: Demurrage / detention / storage: recovered ÷ paid out, direct files only. This layer is fully reliable (100% of demurrage payables hang off the house bill). Below 80% is red. Above 100% is not an error — rebills often carry a markup, and what was recovered may not belong to the same period as what was paid.
op.dupGroupsHelp: Groups where an identical charge line (vendor + invoice no + description + rate + qty) on this file was entered on more than one voucher. This is a **lead for someone to check against the original vendor invoice, not a verdict that this person overpaid** — without the vendor invoice total as an anchor, legitimate split entry on a consolidated bill looks exactly like duplicate entry. Drill in for the entry gap: a gap near zero usually means one batch of work; hours or days apart is what deserves a look.
op.arBilledHelp: Total receivable invoiced on this person's direct files. A sense of scale, not profit, and not a commission basis.
op.scorecardHelp: One row per operator, attributed by the file's operator field (the person the file belongs to), 99.9% coverage. ⚠ This is a different population from "Staff output" on the Analytics page, which counts by created_by (whoever keyed the record in): 171 operator values vs 189 created_by values, only 149 overlapping — the numbers on the two pages should not be compared. Click a name to focus the trend chart below.
op.trendHelp: Bars = files opened (dark = direct, light = agency); line = median billing lag of that month's direct files. ⚠ The last month or two reads artificially low: only invoiced files have a lag, and files opened this month but not yet invoiced are not in the denominator — don't read it as improvement.

issueHelp.unbilled: Direct files with payable cost incurred and no receivable at all, opened more than 45 days ago. These are the ones to chase now.
issueHelp.slow_billing: Direct files that were invoiced, but more than 45 days after the file was opened.
issueHelp.unrecovered: Files where cost that should have been rebilled was not, or only partly. Check file by file whether it was missed or contractually agreed.
issueHelp.demurrage: Files that incurred demurrage / detention / storage, showing paid out vs recovered. Watch the ones where paid far exceeds recovered.
issueHelp.duplicate: Leads for suspected duplicate payable entry. Verify against the original vendor invoice — this alone does not prove an overpayment. A gap near zero usually means one batch of work.

op.agentDebitHelp: Amount debited to an overseas agent or affiliate on a credit/debit note (CR/DB). This is the second path for passing cost through — versions before 2026-09-25 could not see it and therefore misread about 60% of normal business as "not rebilled" (94% for duty). Gap = cost − customer receivable − agent debit.
